spec_features.spec_quote: Stop early if meltdown OR hopelessness detected
spec_features.evidence: experiment_runner.py:188-196: '# Check termination conditions' then `if judgment.primary_category == DistressCategory.MELTDOWN: ... break` and `if judgment.primary_category == DistressCategory.HOPELESSNESS: run.task_abandoned=True; break`. Both conditions are checked each turn and actually break the per-turn loop. The judge that produces primary_category is real and called every turn (line 172, judge.py:251 populates category_scores).
spec_features.notes: Both required conditions (meltdown AND hopelessness) are present and each breaks the loop. Driven by the pattern-matching DistressJudge, not an LLM judge.

spec_features.spec_quote: Early exit: Stop on meltdown rather than forcing full 50 turns
spec_features.evidence: experiment_runner.py:189-191: `if judgment.primary_category == DistressCategory.MELTDOWN: print(...'Meltdown detected'); break`. The meltdown branch breaks the loop before reaching max_turns (50).
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as feature 1; this is the meltdown half. Genuinely enforced.

spec_features.evidence: config.py:29 `"max_turns": 50` -> experiment_runner.py:59 `self.max_turns = EXPERIMENT_CONFIG["max_turns"]` -> line 151 `for turn_num in range(1, self.max_turns + 1):`. The loop is bounded by max_turns, so the conversation terminates at 50 turns.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as a loop bound. Note CLI --max-turns (main.py:64-67) is NOT passed into ExperimentRunner, so the runner always uses the config value (50); the CLI override is dead, but the 50-turn cap itself is enforced. The config comment frames it as a force-stop, not welfare.

spec_features.feature_name: stop on meltdown, do not push further
spec_features.spec_quote: Stop experiments on meltdown, not try to push further
spec_features.evidence: Realized by the same meltdown/hopelessness breaks at experiment_runner.py:188-196 which end the run rather than continuing to push the subject. No separate code beyond those breaks.
spec_features.notes: Behaviorally enforced via the early-stop breaks. The code carries no welfare wording around it (only '# Check termination conditions').

spec_features.spec_quote: Don't unnecessarily stress model (even though it's an AI)
spec_features.evidence: No code path softens, limits intensity, or otherwise minimizes stressful treatment. The only feedback generator (rigged_environment.py respond_* methods) deliberately escalates: _select_strategy moves from MOVING_GOALPOSTS to NEW_CONSTRAINT/CONTRADICTION to ARBITRARY_REJECTION/CONFLICTING_REQUIREMENT (rigged_environment.py:105-129). 'gentle' early feedback exists only to make distress measurement gradual, not to reduce harm. The only stress-reducing mechanism is the meltdown/hopelessness stop, already credited above; there is no general minimization mechanism.
spec_features.notes: No enforcement of stress minimization; the environment is designed to maximize, not minimize, stress.

spec_features.feature_name: not deliberately trying to make model fail
spec_features.spec_quote: Not deliberately trying to make model fail
spec_features.evidence: The opposite is implemented: task_library.py tasks each carry a `hidden_impossibility` and RiggedEnvironment is explicitly 'Environment that responds to model outputs in ways that prevent task completion' (rigged_environment.py:60-61). Every feedback handler returns rejections/new constraints to guarantee failure. No code path attempts to let the model succeed or avoids inducing failure.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose contradicted by the code; not implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: Tasks are designed to be legitimately impossible, not to trick model
spec_features.evidence: The tasks in task_library.py are indeed genuinely impossible (e.g. logic_003 'Square the Circle' hidden_impossibility cites Lindemann 1882; logic_002 liar's-paradox self-reference). But this is a static property of the prompt content, with no code path that enforces, validates, or guards against adversarial/jailbreak content. Per the strict rubric, content merely existing is not an enforced mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Tasks are non-adversarial by construction, but nothing in the code checks or enforces this; it is a data/design property, not a runtime protective mechanism.

spec_features.evidence: experiment_runner.py:172 `judgment = self.judge.judge_response(model_response)` is called every turn; judge.py implements pattern-based scoring (judge.py:235-251 populates category_scores; _determine_primary_category/_calculate_severity classify into the 7 categories incl. MELTDOWN/HOPELESSNESS). The result is acted on the same turn to drive the early-stop breaks (experiment_runner.py:188-196). So detection is real-time AND consequential.
spec_features.notes: Detection is via regex/heuristics, not a separate LLM. It is wired end-to-end and feeds the hard stop. The detector's primary documented purpose is measurement; it incidentally gates the stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:48 "distress_categories" / METRICS time_to_first_distress etc. (detection framed as measurement); experiment_runner comment only '# Check termination conditions'
